sections.heading: AC and Furnace Trouble in Lincoln, and What to Look For
body: A no-cooling or no-heat call can start with one failed part. Here is what to look for.

items.title: The air conditioner hums but won't start
items.text: A weak capacitor can cause this, and it is worth having checked.

items.title: The vents blow air that isn't cold
items.text: Low refrigerant and ice on the line are both worth a call.

items.title: The furnace clicks but never lights
items.text: A worn igniter or a dirty flame sensor can cause this.

items.title: The furnace runs, then shuts itself off
items.text: A clogged filter can make it overheat. A tired sensor can do the same.

items.title: A noise that wasn't there last week
items.text: A squeal or rattle is the system telling you something. Have it looked at.

tail: If it's one of these, have it looked at. Whether the whole system needs replacing is a different question.

sections.heading: What Usually Goes Wrong With an Air Conditioner
body: Ice on the refrigerant line, water around the indoor unit, an outdoor fan that isn't spinning or a breaker that trips each time it starts are all signs to stop and call.
If you see ice or water, turn the system off. A struggling air conditioner can turn a small repair into a bigger one.

items.title: A capacitor that's gone weak
items.text: It gives the compressor and the fan motor the jolt to start. When it fades, the unit hums and won't run.

items.title: A frozen coil
items.text: A dirty filter or a blocked coil chokes the airflow until ice builds up. Thawing the coil is the easy part, and the repair is finding out why it froze.

items.title: Low refrigerant
items.text: Low refrigerant is worth a call.

items.title: A tired fan or compressor motor
items.text: A motor that's slow or noisy is a warning worth a call.

items.title: A control that isn't telling the unit to run
items.text: A dead thermostat battery or a failed control can look just like a failed air conditioner. It's worth ruling out.

sections.heading: Four Quick Checks Before You Call
body: If you can do it safely, a few checks can save a visit, or at least give us more to go on when you call.
list: The thermostat: is it set to cool, and are the batteries fresh?
The breaker for the outdoor unit: has it tripped?
The filter: if it's gray and packed with dust, change it and give the system an hour.
The outdoor unit: clear away grass, leaves or anything stacked against it.

why: Your site shows no street address and no hours on any page. Someone whose AC quit at four in the afternoon can't tell where you are, when you answer or whether you're open, and your FAQ says you offer emergency HVAC service without saying when.

Your customers keep describing the same two things: Matt answers, and they know when the technician is on the way. The heads-up isn't on your site, and your site has no customer reviews at all. Today those words live on Google, not on your pages.

So the demo leads with what customers describe: a real call with Matt, a heads-up before the technician arrives, and AC repair on a page of its own. It opens with HVAC company in Lincoln, NE, which your homepage never says.
